turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Mr. Brennan, come on in. Your wife went back to the waiting room. She told me you've been asking the same questions over and over, and that you got lost driving home from the hardware store last week. Blood pressure is one thirty-eight over eighty-two, pulse seventy-six, oxygen ninety-seven percent.

[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Lost? I wasn't lost. And I don't repeat myself. I'm fine. The parking lot's the problem, some guy in a red truck took two spots, and the magazines out there are six months old.

[SEG0003] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): She left a medication list with me. It says lisinopril ten milligrams every morning, atorvastatin twenty milligrams at bedtime, and baby aspirin, eighty-one milligrams, once a day. I'll tell Dr. Shah you're set.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Lisinopril is twenty, she bumped it, and Margaret fusses. I used to fish every Saturday— well, actually Sundays, Saturday was errands. Bass, mostly.
[SEG0005] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hi, I'm Dr. Shah. So the note from your wife is memory, repeating questions and getting turned around. You're telling me that's off?

[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah it's off. I'm sharp. I do the crossword, not the Sunday one, that one's mean. I ask her what day it is once, because the calendar's in the kitchen and I'm in my chair. Once. Not over and over.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the hardware store, she said you got lost on the way home last week.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): I knew where I was. Construction on Oak, so I went around by the school. Longer, not lost. I used to deliver mail for the post office, thirty years, I don't get lost.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): What about appointments? Has one slipped by you?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, the dentist, yeah, I missed that. The card got shoved under a pile of mail. Their fish tank is huge, clownfish, the whole thing. One time. That's not a pattern.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): When did this start, the missed appointment, her worrying? Weeks, months?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): I couldn't tell you. Maybe since winter? Or it could've been before that. I don't keep a diary, time just slips.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): Do you search for words, like the word is there and won't come out?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really. I talk plenty, you can tell. My grandson says I tell the same fishing story, but that's because it's a good story.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any headaches, any falls, any weakness in an arm or a leg?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No headaches. No falls. Arms and legs are fine, I walked in. That hallway carpet is something else, though.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Your wife handles the medicines, from what I can see.

[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): She fills the weekly box Sunday night, in front of the TV. I take what's in there. The blood pressure one is lisinopril, twenty milligrams, she told me they raised it. Then the cholesterol pill at night, and the little aspirin. I don't fight the box.

[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): Her list says lisinopril ten milligrams, not twenty. I'm not going to pick a winner in here. The atorvastatin twenty at bedtime and the aspirin eighty-one daily do match what you just said, so I'll go with those.

[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Ten, twenty, she handles it, I just swallow. Oh— last spring at the other clinic they checked my sugar and they said it was borderline. I still eat pie. She can live with that.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Borderline is all we've got, not an actual number. Any allergies to medicines, any reactions?

[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing I'm allergic to. Never had a problem with penicillin or anything. A new laundry soap gave me a rash years ago, but that's not a medicine, the soap was just strong.

[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): Okay. Let me think out loud. I'm not putting a name on the memory piece today, I don't have one. What I want is bloodwork, the screen we do when memory is the question, and a proper memory assessment. Then we'll know more than a story from the hallway.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Needles. My veins hide, last time the girl had to stick me twice. Is the memory thing a quiz? I was fine at quizzes. Geography, not so much.

[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): More a structured memory assessment than a quiz, and the desk will book it. I'll order the bloods today, blood count, metabolic panel, B12, thyroid, and a glucose, because that old one was only called borderline. No need to fast unless the lab says so.
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Glucose again. If they want it borderline they can write it on a cake. I told Margaret twenty minutes. She worries, and she hides the good cookies, which is just rude.

[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): Almost done. I'd like you to let her drive until we've finished that memory assessment. Not forever, just for now. And come back in about three weeks, when the bloods are back and the assessment is lined up.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): She already takes the keys half the time. Fine. Three weeks. Can you tell her about the lisinopril so she quits saying I'm the one who's wrong?

[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'll write down both doses and we'll sort lisinopril with her list and the pharmacy, not by guessing. If you get more confused, or you fall, don't wait the three weeks, call us. Otherwise I'll see you in about three weeks.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Call if I fall, got it. I still remember every porch on Maple, thirty years of routes. That should count for something, right?
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): It counts for a lot. It just doesn't answer today's question, which is why we're testing and not deciding anything in this room. Anything you wanted to ask me?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): What day is the memory thing? And— wait, did I already ask you that? No, I didn't. See, I don't repeat.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): No date yet. The front desk will call you with the memory assessment time, and the lab can draw you today or tomorrow, whenever you can sit still. That's my part done.
[SEG0034] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I can walk you out to your wife. Lab's down the hall if you want those bloods today. I'll put the return visit on the books for about three weeks.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Tell her I behaved. And I'm fine. Mostly. If that red truck is still hogging two spots, that's the actual emergency.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): We'll tell her the plan. Not a diagnosis, I don't have one to give. Take care, Mr. Brennan.

features: test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.

omissions.text: Lisinopril dose is incompletely/wrongly recorded: staff list said 10 mg every morning, but the patient twice stated lisinopril had been increased to 20 mg and Dr. said both doses would be written down and reconciled with the wife’s list and the pharmacy rather than guessing.
Possible word-finding difficulty was discussed: patient said he sometimes has trouble getting a word out ('sometimes, not really').
Time course of the memory concern was uncertain beyond the missed appointment: patient said his wife's worrying/memory issues may have been since winter or even before, and that time slips.
Medication management detail: wife fills a weekly pill box on Sunday night and handles his medicines; patient takes what is in the box.

Allergy history detail omitted: patient denied medication allergies and specifically said he has never had a problem with penicillin; he reported a non-medication rash from a new laundry soap years ago.
Doctor explicitly said no diagnosis/name would be assigned to the memory problem today and that testing was being done before deciding anything.
Additional plan detail: blood tests could be drawn today or tomorrow, and there was no need to fast unless the lab said so.
Follow-up scheduling detail: the front desk would call with the memory assessment appointment time.
